items.title: 53279_Lee Young Oral History Interview
items.q: my father in law, Mr. Nelson, who owned the Dunbar Hotel; he gave one

ctx.x: So that's the way that they would get the facilities or whatever they needed to get -- whether it was uniforms or something like that, and it's just so strange the way history repeats itself, because I used to fool with kids here in Los Angeles, with baseball and basketball, and I remember one time that I had a baseball team, and we had 13 kids on the team and I wanted to get some uniforms for them, and you know, I'm speaking of Los Angeles -- and they had a lot of doctors and lawyers and professional people, and…

Well, I'll never forget that I only got 4 uniforms, and 3 of them were from for like, guys, like Black Dot McGee, and he gave one, and Sonny Howard gave one, and J.B. Brown, and then my father in law, Mr. Nelson, who owned the Dunbar Hotel; he gave one, but other than that, I had to pay for them myself.
So I guess, things don't change too drastically, you know?
